title: artifact download cleanup: remove_on_error must re-raise the original error even when removing the partial file fails
answers: Artifact download fails with Permission denied on a file in the destination folder instead of the real download error
Why does a failed download or virtualenv creation hide the root cause behind a cleanup error?
Where is the partial-download cleanup on error handled?
Why does the log say the partial file was removed when it was never created?
body:
Path: mlflow/utils/file_utils.py:remove_on_error, a context manager wrapping partial-output writes. Used when artifact downloads fail (HttpArtifactRepository._multipart_download, CloudArtifactRepository._parallelized_download_from_cloud, DatabricksModelsArtifactRepository) and when _create_virtualenv fails; it deletes the partial file or directory, then propagates the failure.
Rule: Keep the cleanup in its own try/except inside the except block. Dispatch to os.remove for regular files or shutil.rmtree for directories, log "Successfully removed" only after that call returns, and log a cleanup failure as "Failed to remove <path>: <err>" without raising. Always end with a bare `raise` so the original exception object and traceback propagate. Paths that are neither a regular file nor a directory are logged as "Not removing" and left alone.
Symptom: A download that failed for a real reason (for example chunks exhausted retries) surfaced as "[Errno 13] Permission denied" on the partial file in the destination directory, because the read-only directory made cleanup raise and replaced the original error. Separately, an empty destination with no file created still logged "Successfully removed <path>".
Constraints: Behaviour is unchanged when cleanup succeeds, so happy paths of the callers are not affected. Do not change the callers to swallow or re-wrap errors; fix belongs in remove_on_error. Tests that exercise this are in tests/utils/test_file_utils.py (test_remove_on_error_*), and they assert the exact list of warnings emitted.
applies: Any code using remove_on_error in mlflow/utils/file_utils.py, including artifact download and virtualenv creation error paths; not general file deletion helpers.
says: Artifact download fails with Permission denied on a file in the destination folder instead of the real error
Failed download or virtualenv creation hides the root cause behind a cleanup error
Log says partial file was removed when no file was ever created
search: Partial-output cleanup on error in remove_on_error: the cleanup runs in its own try block, the original exception is always re-raised even if removing the partial file or directory fails, and it logs removal only after a successful delete. Paths that are neither a regular file nor a directory are logged as not removed. Applies to artifact downloads and virtualenv creation, not general file deletion.
